title: Intake & Prioritization Framework for Private/VPC/On‑Prem Deployment Requests (networking, upgrades, air‑gapped)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: We need a repeatable intake and prioritization framework for incoming Private / VPC / on‑prem customer requests that surface networking constraints, upgrade windows, and air‑gapped compatibility. Current ad‑hoc handling causes delays, uneven tradeoffs, and missed SLA expectations. This ticket defines a rubric, decision flow, and operational checklist for PMs and Solutions Eng to triage non‑bug feature/config requests from enterprise customers.

Background: Over the last 9 months we have seen 40+ inbound items that overlap networking (VPC peering, firewall/NAT, allowed egress), upgrade cadence (minor vs major, staging pathways), and air‑gapped constraints (no outbound internet, repo mirroring, signed binaries). Each request currently follows a mix of email, Slack, and ad‑hoc Google forms. We need a single source workflow that: collects consistent data, scores requests by cost/risk/strategic value, and outputs clear outcomes (fasttrack, engineering intake, pay‑for‑work, or not‑planned).

Goals:
- Reduce time from intake to decision to <= 5 business days for high‑impact enterprise requests.
- Provide transparent scoring so customers and sales know why an ask is prioritized.
- Surface non‑functional blockers (network, airgap, upgrade policy) early to avoid rework.
- Define handoffs between PM, Solutions Eng, Security, and Eng squads.

Proposed intake form fields (minimum viable):
- Customer name and account ID
- Brief description of requested capability (free text)
- Category: networking | upgrade | air‑gapped | compliance | other
- Expected ROI / business driver (product launch, compliance, contract)
- SLA need: uptime/latency/throughput targets
- Environment: Hosted | Dedicated | Private/VPC | On‑prem air‑gapped
- Network topology constraints: egress allowed? IP whitelisting? Private peering?
- Maintenance window constraints and upgrade blackout periods
- Data residency and encryption/KMS requirements
- Willingness to pay (billable engagement / custom engineering budget)
- Requested timeline (date)
- Attachments: network diagrams, SOC/IT docs, security contacts

Scoring rubric (0–10 per axis, automated calculation):
- Strategic value (0–10): Is customer strategic / referenceable / expansion revenue?
- Operational risk (0–10): Probability of blocking production or causing incidents if unsupported. Higher is worse.
- Implementation cost (0–10): Estimated ENG weeks to deliver (converted to score).
- Compliance urgency (0–10): Legal/regulatory deadline proximity.
- Workability under air‑gap (0–10): Higher score = more complex.
Total score drives bucket: Fasttrack (>=35), Planned (25–34), Needs Costing (15–24), Low Priority / Not Planned (<15).

Decision outcomes and definitions:
- Fasttrack: High score, low engineering cost, and security signoff possible within 5 days. Target SLA: decision within 2 business days, delivery via Solutions Eng + runbook.
- Planned: Allocate to next private deployment sprint or rollout window. Requires scoping ticket with ENG and scheduling.
- Needs Costing: Requires formal SOW/paid engagement; PM to route to Sales/Professional Services.
- Not Planned: Low strategic value and high cost. Provide written rationale and alternative recommendations.

Operational checklist for triage (PM + SE):
1) Verify intake completeness; request missing diagrams/contacts.
2) Quick security gating: does this touch cryptographic material, KMS, or private keys? If yes, tag security_review_required=true and notify Security.
3) Network compatibility check: can request be satisfied via existing VPC peering or does it require NAT/eBPF proxies or customer changes?
4) Upgrade path assessment: can new runtime be delivered as a minor/patch? Does on‑prem package support rolling upgrades?
5) Air‑gap feasibility: enumerate artifacts that must be mirrored and estimate automation effort.
6) Estimate implementation effort (SE + ENG) and cost bucket.
7) Produce decision email to customer with next steps and expected timelines.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Fast resolution vs. thorough security review: we will enforce a security gating step for anything touching keys or admin planes which may extend decision time.
- Standardizing on a scoring threshold may deprioritize niche but high‑value compliance requests; ensure manual override process with Exec signoff.

Example triage scenarios (illustrative):
- Customer A (large fintech) requests Private with egress blocked and KMS integration for PII processing, willing to pay for engineering: Scores high on strategic and compliance urgency -> Needs Costing -> propose SOW.
- Customer B requests one‑off IP whitelisting for a temporary proof of concept: Low strategic value, low cost -> Fasttrack via Solutions Eng runbook.

Acceptance criteria: the intake form is live in Confluence + Google Form, scoring automation in Linear custom field, and an internal playbook published in the Console Docs.

Metrics to evaluate success: time-to-decision, % of requests routed to correct outcome, customer satisfaction on SLA, backlog carryover month‑over‑month.

Risks: inaccurate initial estimates may lead to scope creep; dependency on Security review turnaround; engineering capacity spikes. Mitigation: require customer signoff on SOW for paid work, and a 2‑week SLAT for Security review for prioritized items.
acceptance_criteria: Intake template published in Confluence with required fields
Linear custom fields created: intake_score (integer), outcome_bucket (string)
Playbook created and linked in Console Docs describing triage flow and handoffs
Two pilot requests routed through process with documented outcomes and retrospective
